title: Signed operation logs enable post-hoc safety auditing beyond sandboxes
content:
## Claim

Sandboxes, permission prompts, and filters are preventative. They cannot answer post-hoc questions such as which skill exfiltrated data or whether provenance matches access policy.

A signed operation log carrying actor, skill, inputs read, and state written makes those questions decidable. Compromised or divergent skill versions leave detectable traces against expected reducer output.

## Co-signing

High-stakes workflows can co-sign actions with input state hash or previous operation ID so swapped context between dispatch and execution fails to apply.

## Scope of claim

Provenance does not prevent attacks; it makes them attributable so defense is not guesswork.

## Methodology grounding
The claims below live in the plugin's `data/methodology/` corpus; the relationship is stated per claim.

- **[[agent session boundaries create natural automation checkpoints that human-operated systems lack]]** — BUILDS_ON. That claim locates enforcement at lifecycle boundaries, where a check fires because the event happened rather than because anyone remembered. A signed operation log extends the same logic past the session: the record is auditable after the fact, so a boundary that was never instrumented can still be examined.
- **[[hook enforcement guarantees quality while instruction enforcement merely suggests it]]** — RELATES_TO. A sandbox instructs; a signature guarantees. The methodology's distinction between enforcement and suggestion is the same one that separates a permission prompt from an immutable signed record.
description: Preventative controls intervene at action time; signed logs make exfiltration, credential access, and supply-chain skill divergence attributable after the fact.
